definitions.explanation: A tall, large-flowered iris with sword-shaped leaves, planted in damp gardens and along stream banks. Blooms June through early July in a wide range of cultivated colors.

{花菖蒲|はなしょうぶ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{梅雨|つゆ}→梅雨：02232_tsuyu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時期|じき}→時期：03269_jiki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見頃|みごろ}→見頃：16868_migoro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧。
examples.english: Japanese irises reach their peak during the rainy season.

examples.english: Japanese irises come in regional cultivar groups — Edo, Ise, Higo — each with its own characteristics.

notes:
Often confused with アヤメ and ⟦{杜若|かきつばた}→杜若：28744_kakitsubata⟧ (rabbitear iris). The dividing rule of thumb: {花菖蒲|はなしょうぶ} is the tallest and is grown on damp land, ⟦{杜若|かきつばた}→杜若：28744_kakitsubata⟧ grows in shallow water, and アヤメ prefers drier soil.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{杜若|かきつばた}→杜若：28744_kakitsubata⟧: rabbitear iris — water-grown; smaller; blooms slightly earlier
- アヤメ: Siberian iris — drier soil; smaller flowers
- {菖蒲|しょうぶ}: sweet flag — different plant entirely; the iris is the "⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧" (flowering) version of the name only

In the iris-festival custom on ⟦{端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}→端午の節句：16518_tangonosekku⟧ (Boys' Day, May 5), it is the leaves of {菖蒲|しょうぶ} (sweet flag), not {花菖蒲|はなしょうぶ}, that are used in the bath.
